fatal_errors: No specific material is identified; the target material is the Re-containing Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 refractory high-entropy-alloy film.
The essential comparison between NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWRe before and after He implantation is absent.
The proposed dislocation–grain-boundary mechanism misses the target irradiation-defect-sink mechanism and suppression of He-bubble growth and segregation.
No cited or quantitative evidence supports the claim.
explanation: The hypothesis only makes a generic statement that engineered grain boundaries may improve ductility. It weakly overlaps with the target through the relevance of grain boundaries, but it does not reconstruct the Re addition, nanocrystalline BCC sputtered-film state, 120 keV He irradiation conditions, amorphous boundary regions, defect annihilation, or the observed reductions in irradiation hardening and grain-boundary embrittlement. Its proposed experiment could assess a broad grain-boundary/ductility correlation, but it is not designed to distinguish the target Re-mediated helium-damage mechanism.
